summary: The note traces the history of community Chronic Disease Management and Prevention Workshops, starting with the first one in Somerville on Sept 5th, 2023, led by Dr. Emily Steward. It describes the holistic workshop model, its replication in other places, the addition of mental health components and the later digital transformation. It concludes that the workshops now influence national campaigns, schools, workplaces and local policy.
one_line: History of Somerville's chronic disease management workshops, from Dr. Emily Steward's 2023 launch to mental health and digital integration and wider influence.
key_facts: The first Chronic Disease Management and Prevention Workshop in the area was held on Sept 5th, 2023, at the local community center in Somerville.
Dr. Emily Steward, a public health advocate, spearheaded the initiative to address soaring rates of chronic diseases in the community.
The workshop was funded by a grant secured through the Somerville Health Foundation.
The workshops targeted chronic diseases such as diabetes, heart disease, and respiratory conditions.
The curriculum moved from theoretical education to practical skills such as meal planning, reading nutrition labels, physical activity regimes, and stress management techniques.
Nutritionist Linda Myers and fitness expert Coach Jim Thompson helped Dr. Steward create the curriculum.
By late 2023, multiple health departments and community organizations had begun to replicate the Somerville model.
Phoebe Martín, a Somerville resident with type 2 diabetes, became the poster child for the workshops after a significant turnaround in her health.
Facilitators later integrated psychological components such as coping strategies, mindfulness exercises, and peer support groups, with mentors like clinical psychologist Jonathan McGill.
The workshops introduced virtual reality programs simulating supermarkets to teach about food choices, and apps for medication adherence.
Emily 'EJ' Jackson, with a background in health informatics, joined in 2024 and helped create an online portal serving as an information repository and interactive community.
The workshops have paved the way for national health campaigns and are now integrated into schools, workplaces, and local policy-making.
